ruleName: Four-Ball: Wrong Number of Strokes Given
imagePrompt: A semi-realistic, modern, and polished illustration (about 75% realistic, 25% stylised) in a junior golf quiz style. Depict a golf green with four players: one (Daniel) holding his putter and looking surprised or concerned after realising a mistake, another player (an opponent) offering a conceding gesture such as a handshake. The other two players (Daniel’s partner and the second opponent) stand close by, visually involved in the moment. Golf balls are near the hole to show the hole is nearly finished. The scene should show the subtle tension of the rules situation. Do not include any text, labels, numbers, arrows, captions, diagrams, badges, logos, watermarks, club crests, scorecards, or speech bubbles.
imageAlt: On a green, four players gather as one golfer looks surprised after an opponent makes a conceding gesture, with all four balls near the hole.

sceneSpec.setting: A well-kept putting green on a golf course during a match.
sceneSpec.players: Four players: Daniel (still on the green, looking thoughtful), Daniel’s partner nearby, and two opponents (one offering a congratulatory gesture as if conceding the hole).
sceneSpec.ballPosition: Daniel’s ball is near the hole on the green. The other balls are nearby, indicating the hole is being completed.
sceneSpec.ruleMoment: The moment just after Daniel’s opponent concedes the hole, and Daniel realises he gave the wrong number of strokes.
sceneSpec.educationalFocus: Highlight the importance of giving the correct number of strokes in four-ball and the penalty for providing incorrect information leading to a concession.
mustShow: Daniel holding a putter and looking surprised or concerned
An opponent making a conceding gesture (such as a handshake offer)
All four players present around the green

questions.title: Telling the wrong score in four-ball
questions.question: In a four-ball team game, Daniel's opponent asks, 'How many shots have you played?' Daniel says 'three', so the opponent gives up (concedes) the hole. But Daniel then remembers he actually took four shots. What is the right thing to do?

choices.text: The score counts and nothing happens.
Daniel gets two extra shots, but the score counts.

questions.explanation: If you say the wrong number of shots and your opponent makes a choice because of it, your team loses the hole. It's important to always say the right score in four-ball.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A team game where two players play their own ball and the best score counts for the team.
To let the other player or team win the hole without finishing.
A shot or hit of the ball.

questions.teachingTip: Remind kids to count their shots out loud or on their fingers to be sure of their score before saying it to anyone.
likelyMisconceptions: Thinking you can just correct your score after the hole is over.
Thinking the hole doesn't count and should be played again.

questions.title: Giving the wrong number of strokes in four-ball
questions.question: In a four-ball match, Daniel is asked by an opponent how many strokes he has taken. Daniel says three and his opponent concedes the hole. Daniel then realises he had actually taken four strokes. What is the ruling?

choices.text: The concession stands and there is no penalty.
Daniel is penalised two strokes but the concession stands.

questions.explanation: In four-ball match play, if a player gives a wrong number of strokes taken that affects an opponent’s understanding of the match situation, their side loses the hole (Rule 23.8a(2)).
